title: Existence/explicit construction of the chain: exhibit transition rule P(mu,nu) via local moves not referencing F*_mu

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Sub-lemma (L1).** The problem is an existence question ("Does there exist a nontrivial Markov chain..."). The first substantive step is to **exhibit** the chain: give explicit transition probabilities $P(\mu,\nu)$ for $\mu,\nu\in S_n(\lambda)$ in closed form in $t$ and the $x_i$, built from **local moves** (ASEP-type hops, a single-row *decrement* move, and a *merge/sort* move), together with a holding probability.

**Nontriviality constraint (must be checked, L5).** By the problem's definition, the transition probabilities may **not** be described using the polynomials $F^*_\mu$. Hence the naive choice $P(\mu,\nu)\propto F^*_\nu$ is forbidden; the construction must be genuinely local/combinatorial.

Deliverable: a fully written-out transition kernel (no placeholders), from which q3-5 (row-stochasticity), the stationarity bridge $\pi P=\pi$, and q3-6 (irreducibility/aperiodicity) can be verified. No current open issue isolates the *construction* itself; the open issues all critique steps of an assumed kernel.
